summary: Lists more ssh connection parameters: pkcs11_provider for smartcards, port, private_key (PEM contents, needs SSH_AGENT, 2.19), private_key_file, private_key_passphrase (only with private_key), reconnection_retries (only on rc 255), remote_user, scp_executable, scp_extra_args, sftp_batch_mode, and sftp_executable.
questions: How do I use a smartcard / PKCS11 key with Ansible SSH?
How do I make Ansible retry SSH connections?
Can I pass the private key contents instead of a file path?
Why doesn't private_key_passphrase work with my key file?
What user does Ansible log in as if I don't set remote_user?
How do I point Ansible at a different scp or sftp binary?

answer_card.title: ssh connection parameters (part 2)
answer_card.answer_md:
- `pkcs11_provider` (2.12): SmartCard provider, e.g. `/usr/local/lib/opensc-pkcs11.so`.
- `port`: remote port.
- `private_key` (2.19): key contents in PEM; requires `SSH_AGENT` config enabled.
- `private_key_file`: path to the key file.
- `private_key_passphrase` (2.19): only for `private_key`; has **no effect** with `private_key_file`.
- `reconnection_retries` (default 0): retries happen only on ssh return code 255; other codes mean a program execution issue.
- `remote_user`: login user (usually from the `remote_user` keyword); if unset, the ssh client chooses.
- `scp_executable` / `sftp_executable` (default `scp` / `sftp` from `$PATH`), `scp_extra_args`.
- `sftp_batch_mode` (default true): batch mode allows detection of transfer errors.
